title: Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards for Human-Behavior Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2611.28048v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate survey respondents in social-science research. A useful simulator should predict individual responses, reproduce population response distributions, and capture demographic differences. Common training approaches struggle to balance these goals: exact-match rewards encourage the model to concentrate on the most frequent human response, which is contradictory to the goal of distributional alignment. Meanwhile, aggregate distribution matching can look good even when demographic information is ignored. To this end, we introduce Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards (DVR), a reinforcement-learning reward that uses demographic group distribution gaps to guide individual responses, designed by aligning policy generated frequencies with human response frequencies within each question-group margins. translated_title: 用于人类行为模拟的分布可验证奖励
translated_abstract: 大语言模型在社会科学研究中越来越多地被用于模拟调查受访者。一个有用的模拟器应该能够预测个体回答、重现总体回答分布，并捕捉人口统计学差异。常见的训练方法难以平衡这些目标：精确匹配奖励会促使模型集中于最频繁出现的人类回答，这与分布对齐的目标相矛盾；而聚合分布匹配即使在忽略人口统计信息的情况下也可能看起来表现良好。为此，我们提出了分布可验证奖励（DVR），这是一种强化学习奖励，通过在每个问题-群体边界内将策略生成的回答频率与人类回答频率对齐，利用人口群体分布差距来指导个体回答的生成。我们使用 OpinionQA 数据集对该方法进行评估，发现与仅使用准确率的方法相比……
tldr: 提出了分布可验证奖励（DVR），一种利用人口群体分布差距指导个体回答的强化学习奖励方法，使大语言模型在模拟调查受访者时能同时兼顾个体预测准确性、总体分布对齐和人口统计差异的捕捉。
en_tdlr: Introduces Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards (DVR), a reinforcement-learning reward that uses demographic group distribution gaps to guide individual responses, enabling LLMs to simulate survey respondents while balancing individual prediction accuracy, distributional alignment, and demographic differences.
